By comparison, this ratio peaked at 6.4% during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.

The US equity market's bull run shows no signs of slowing down:

The S&P 500 has recorded 124 all-time highs since the current bull market began on October 12th, 2022.

Over this period, the index has rallied +118%, entering the 5th year of its bull market.

This year alone, the index has posted 28 all-time highs, after 39 and 57 in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

By comparison, the S&P 500 recorded 70 all-time highs in 2021 and 33 in 2020.

Meanwhile, more than 1,003 trading days have passed since the S&P 500 last recorded a new 52-week low, marking the # such streak in history.

For perspective, such a streak lasted 2,556 days between 1990 and 2000, ending on November 21st.

Q4 and post-midterm seasonality remain overwhelmingly bullish.
Historically, the fourth quarter has been the strongest quarter of the year for the S&P 500 in terms of consistency of positive returns. Over roughly the past 80 years, Q4 has produced a positive return about 80% of the time, compared with approximately 60%–64% for the other three quarters.
The midterm election cycle adds another powerful seasonal tailwind. Stocks have historically performed particularly well as the uncertainty surrounding midterm elections is removed. Depending on the precise starting period used, recent historical studies put the S&P 500's positive rate during Q4 of midterm years at roughly 83%–85%.
